blocks.text: Approved with Amendments on May 12, 2025
Keysville Town Council Meeting Minutes
The Town Council meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday, April 14, 2025, at the Keysville Town Office. The following Town Council members were present:
Council Members Mayor Robert Schaefer present: Vice Mayor Anthony Ferranto
Mrs. Rhonda Benn
Mr. Danny Cooper
Mr. Scotty Jackson
Mr. Tom Fisher
Council Members Mrs. Wendy Gallion
absent
Town staff Ms. Sherry Marker, Town Clerk
present
Guests present: Jim Benn (Charlotte County Board of Supervisors)
Lynn Duffey, Fire Chief (KVFD)
Eric Traywick
Mayor Schaefer called the meeting to order. Council Member Benn offered the invocation.
Public Comments
Fire Chief Duffey said he would demonstrate the new tool that the town paid for at the next council meeting.
Guest Speaker
Mr. Benn handed out and went over the Charlotte County Planning Commission 2024 Annual Report.
Minutes
Motion to approve March 10, 2025 minutes was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Jackson. Motion was carried unanimously.
Financials
Motion was made by Council Member Fisher and seconded by Council Member Cooper to approve the March 2025 financials and pay the bills. Motion was carried unanimously.
Committees
Street and Library
Council Member Benn gave a list of potholes and roads that need to be repaired.
From Burger King down to Mr. Cooper’s house at 780 King St.
On Osborne Street, D lane and J street
Hill Avenue – pass Tail Waggers to the pothole in front of Greg Chiles house
From Jimmy Ramsey to cut over to Route 59 there is a pothole
At the railroad crossing, spikes are coming up and there are also potholes forming
Potholes behind the post office
Intersection of I Street and the Methodist Church on Church Street.
Mayor Schaefer said a letter to VDOT from the town council needs to be sent regarding the above repairs and pictures need to be sent as well.
Mayor Schaefer said he will get a quote from Virginia Paving and Seal Coating for repairing the roads and potholes that the town is to maintain.
Tower Park Playground

Council Member Benn said she would like to set up a meeting with her contact Mitch Reno with Gametime to have maintenance done on the park to get it up to code and purchase playground equipment that had been budgeted for years but never been spent.
Mayor Schaefer said before we purchase the playground equipment, we need to repair the equipment that is already there and put down mulch and get a quote for maintaining the equipment.
Motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Cooper to get a quote on repairing the existing equipment and getting a contract. Motion was carried unanimously.
Water
Council Member Jackson said he tried reaching out to the water plant, but no one ever answered the phone.
Vice Mayor Ferranto said the water/sewer lines were completed at Habitat for Humanity.
Chief Duffey said he would like to see the fire hydrants color coded.
Wastewater
Council Member Fisher said he had visited the wastewater plant three times since the last meeting.

Mayor Schaefer said Angie from the wastewater plant had done some research on the drying beds for the sludge. In the overall conclusion, it would cost $500,000 just to start the process. Mayor Schaefer said it was best to keep getting Matthew Sanitation to come and remove the sludge.
Mayor Schaefer said we could use B & B Consultants for an engineer on the upgrades to the wastewater plant.
Old Business

Council Member Jackson commented on the “Welcome to Keysville” sign. He said the sign looked a lot better after being cleaned up. He also said we had discussed in a prior meeting about putting the sign in the roundabout circle facing coming from Farmville. Mayor Schaefer said he had a contact with VDOT and he would find out.
Mayor Schaefer recommended the town adopt the federal holidays (11 holidays per year for the full-time employees.

Motion was made by Council Member Fisher and seconded by Council Member Jackson for the full-time employees to observe the federal holidays effective today, April 14, 2025. Motion was carried unanimously.
Mayor Schaefer said a date for the Budget Workshop needed to be planned. The town council members discussed the date of Wednesday, April 30, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.
New Business
No new business to report.
Mayor’s Report
The Board of Supervisors voted to continue to have town representation.
Mayor Schaefer said he had met with our town attorney, David Watkins, and he approved the Water and Sewer Policy.
Motion was made by Council Member Fisher and seconded by Council Member Jackson to approve the Water and Sewer Policy. Motion was carried unanimously.
Mayor Schaefer that we need to have another sign made at the Tower Park Playground that reads
” Play at your own Risk”.
Mayor Schaefer said there was roughly $31,000 in American Rescue Plan funds remaining.
Mayor Schaefer said we are working on getting our DMV information together so we can begin putting “DMV Stops” on customers who have not paid their personal property.
Mayor Schaefer said that the water tower at the Heartland Industrial Park was the responsibility of the town to maintain and it had not been. He had already received a quote for approximately
$3,000.00 to remove the sediment, making it safe for fire suppression.

Motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Fisher to use the American Rescue Plan funds to have the water tower at the Heartland Industrial Park repaired and maintained. Motion was carried unanimously.
Mayor Schaefer said the fire suppression water tank at Genesis also needed repairing and maintained.

Motion was made by Vice Mayor Ferranto and seconded by Council Member Jackson to use the American Rescue Plan funds to have the fire suppression tank at Genesis repaired and maintained. Motion was carried unanimously.

Mayor Schaefer told the town council of two events that were coming up in town. He said the Pregnancy Support Center would be having a “Walk for Life” in September and the Lions Club would like to have a car show on June 7th, 2025 closing off King Street Road like we do for the Christmas Parade. Mayor Schaefer said Event Applications Form would be sent out.
Motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council member Fisher to apply for the Main Street Affiliation grant. Motion was carried unanimously.
Motion was made by Vice Mayor Ferranto and seconded by Council Member Cooper to adjourn the meeting. Motion was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 8:50 p.m.
Sherry L. Marker, Clerk/Treasurer Robert Schaefer, Mayor
